articles.title: See the agents, set the terms: new visibility and control for personal agents
articles.excerpt: Personal AI agents have changed how users interact with the web, blurring the lines between automated and human traffic. Learn how Cloudflare gives site owners visibility and control to manage personal agent access.
details: Personal agents are the intermediary between humans and the Internet, turning a person’s instructions into requests and actions on websites.
A customer might ask a personal agent to compare products across your site, find support articles, or complete a purchase.

To a site owner, all three interactions show up as automated traffic - and without a clear view of which agents are visiting and what they are doing, it can be difficult to know whether that traffic is helping your business or creating risk.
Blocking agents altogether can feel like the safest choice, but it can mean losing customers.
Better visibility into agent activity allows you to decide what access makes sense for your site.

articles.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
articles.excerpt: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, expanding Codex’s tools for building, understanding, and reviewing code.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-pierre/ Today we're announcing that OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc. (“Pierre”), the company behind Code Storage and a family of standout open-source developer tools.
If you’ve browsed files or reviewed a change in the Codex app, you’ve already used Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries.
We’re excited to work with the Pierre team to build on the Git workflows that developers already rely on and adapt them to how teams work with coding agents.
We’ve seen in our own engineering work how the systems around Git need to evolve as more of that work happens in parallel.
Earlier this week, we shared how we’re scaling Git at OpenAI with Pando, our in-house source control backend for engineers and agents.

articles.title: DevRev delivers autonomous self-service with GPT-6.1 Sol
articles.excerpt: DevRev uses GPT-6.1 Sol to power Computer and Operator, balancing reasoning, speed, and cost for enterprise service.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/devrev-enterprise-self-service/ DevRev built Computer and Operator to help service and operations teams carry even the hardest customer and employee requests through to completion.
Computer and Operator are designed to reason across live data.
Actions are reversible, and answers point back to their sources, explains Ahmed Bashir, DevRev’s chief technology officer.
DevRev combines OpenAI models, including GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol, with its harness for connecting company knowledge and giving teams control over the actions an agent can take.
In DevRev’s Agent Studio, users can describe how they want a tool to behave in a conversation with AI and define parts of its behavior with fixed rules.

articles.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
articles.excerpt: Discover how ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers accelerate CAD, PCB design, simulation, and other workflows across the physical world.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/accelerating-engineering-for-the-physical-world/ Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products.
These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster.
Across these projects, engineers need to bring together mechanical designs, electronics, software, and manufacturing requirements using specialized tools.
We’re teaching models to support that work, from preparing drawings and setting up simulations to coordinating changes across disciplines.
Our goal is to give engineers more time to explore ideas and improve designs.

articles.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
articles.excerpt: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
details: When I last wrote about our DNS propagation pipeline in 2022 , the Zone Builder received about 250 DNS record changes per second.
Today it receives about 700, nearly three times as many, plus about 100 other events, such as zone setting changes.
However, the number of events was never the real problem.
The problem was the kind of work some of those events needed, and how that work grows with the size of a zone.
Some zones now hold more than 20 million records, and we expect them to keep growing toward hundreds of millions.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.excerpt: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.
details: Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection . Your origin stays private, while web application firewall ( WAF ), caching , bot management , and Workers work just as they do for public origins.

In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet.
Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.

Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.

articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.
details: Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report.
This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 - July, August, and September - and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume.

The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One , Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network .
Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%.

Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year.

articles.title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
articles.excerpt: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.
details: You receive a ping: a new critical vulnerability has been disclosed.

Your team scrambles to compare vendor advisories, read technical research, check which systems run the affected software, and answer familiar questions from the business: are we affected, and what are we doing about it?
Another disclosure arrives before that work is finished.

AI is changing both the volume and speed of critical vulnerability discovery. It can analyze large codebases at scale and surface deeply nested flaws that may have existed for years without being found through human review. That discovery momentum will put more pressure on security teams to understand the impact of each disclosure on their infrastructure.

To help security teams prepare, today we’re introducing Zero Wire : a public vulnerability intelligence feed on Cloudflare Radar, bringing the clarity of a news wire service to critical security developments. It helps security leaders and practitioners understand significant vulnerabilities and decide what to do next.

articles.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
articles.excerpt: OpenAI built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/ Security research that once required a separate, sustained investigation for each finding can increasingly be run as a systematic process.
This document explores one of our efforts in this area.
Vulnerability discovery is becoming easier to scale, but prioritization and validation remain operational bottlenecks.
We built a prototype to look for security flaws in the Linux kernel inside a controlled research environment.

Our prototype identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to gain root access.

articles.title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
articles.excerpt: Daybreak Red brings GPT-5.6 Cyber to approved customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) through Amazon Bedrock for authorized cybersecurity work.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/daybreak-red-aws-govcloud/ Building on the availability of Daybreak models on Amazon Bedrock, GPT‑5.6 Cyber is now available to approved customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) through Daybreak Red.
This expansion gives government security teams a new way to apply advanced cybersecurity capabilities within the AWS environments they use to support critical missions.
Daybreak Red provides access to OpenAI’s purpose-trained cybersecurity models for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing.
GPT‑5.6 Cyber can help defenders investigate complex software weaknesses, reproduce vulnerabilities in controlled settings, and develop mitigations.
Qualified security practitioners should review findings and proposed fixes before implementation.

articles.title: How Cisco defends at machine speed with OpenAI
articles.excerpt: Cisco combines network intelligence with OpenAI models to strengthen enterprise security. Learn how it is building more adaptive defenses.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/cisco-cyber/ Cisco builds the networking and security infrastructure that organizations rely on to connect and protect their systems.
As adversaries leverage AI to scale automated attacks and craft exploits at machine-speed, defending enterprise infrastructure must evolve.
Pairing Cisco’s vast network telemetry with frontier AI reasoning gives defenders the toolkit necessary to outpace emerging threats.

OpenAI’s rigorous approach to enterprise data privacy-centered on zero data retention, strict customer data boundaries, and verifiable isolation-means Cisco could confidently deploy frontier intelligence across mission-critical systems without compromising customer priorities or sensitive telemetry.
Connecting network intelligence for stronger defense Cisco’s defense starts where threats move: the network.

articles.title: Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world
articles.excerpt: Louis Erbkamm built the first prototype in his free time. Now GitHub Copilot helps him maintain it alone. The post Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Louis Erbkamm knows his way around Arnis, the smallest town in Germany, but he's never set foot in it.
I know where the shops are. Where the boats are... I know the city pretty well, but I haven't been there yet.

Arnis is also the name of his open source project, which takes real-world data from OpenStreetMap and other sources to turn places you know into Minecraft worlds you can freely explore. Since Louis started Arnis in 2022, it's reached close to 900,000 downloads from GitHub and about 70 contributors.

Louis grew up playing Minecraft and started coding at 13, always looking for ways to bring code into the game. Arnis began as a fun diversion combining Minecraft with geospatial data, and it went on GitHub, where he already kept his side projects. He finished the first prototype within two weeks while on a break from school.

That first version was Python written by hand, built only on OpenStreetMap, and generating a town took a while. He needed somewhere real to test it, so he looked up towns in Germany, where he lives, and found Arnis. A small town helped while early generation was slow.

articles.title: Introducing Images 2.6
articles.excerpt: Images 2.6 brings faster image generation, GIF creation, more precise editing, and new API controls across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.
details: With this, you can bring motion to your images with GIFs - from animating a brand mascot or character to turning a product shot into an eye-catching loop.
You can also create polished visuals faster and refine them with greater precision - keeping characters, products, and brand details consistent as you edit.
People around the world now create 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.
On average, that’s more than half a billion images created per day.
Faster iteration and more professional visuals Images 2.6 generates images 50% faster than before.

articles.title: Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT
articles.excerpt: GitHub’s annual month-long game jam is back for its 14th year! This November, make a game inspired by the theme SHIFT. Change gears, swap perspectives, bend reality, or just press a certain key. The post Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Game Off , GitHub's annual month-long game jam, returns for its 14th year this November. Thousands of developers have joined us over the years to make everything from polished platformers to wonderfully weird experiments.
Whether you're making your first game or your fiftieth, we'd love for you to join us.
Shift gears. Shift perspectives. Shift dimensions. Shift bits. Work the night shift. Or make a game where the only buttons are the Shift keys.
You have until December 1, 2026, at 13:37 PST to build and submit a game inspired by SHIFT. Strong or loose inspirations apply!
A change in position, direction, perspective, or reality.

articles.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
articles.excerpt: Today, we laid out our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive, end-to-end software delivery system in the world. The post GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we've gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn't changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.

Today at GitHub Universe , we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we're rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.
The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment.
A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system.
Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand.
